summary: Adds three optional operations to the Internet Printing Protocol: Set-Job-Attributes and Set-Printer-Attributes for changing job and printer objects, and Get-Printer-Supported-Values for finding what values a printer will accept. It updates RFCs 2910 and 2911.

eli5.summary: Sometimes you want to change a print job or a printer's settings after sending it. These extras let you do that and ask the printer what choices it allows.

questions: how to change ipp job attributes
how to change a print job after submitting

subtitle: Three optional IPP operations that let you change a print job or printer after the fact, and ask a printer what it will accept.

tldr.problem: IPP/1.1 had no standard way to change a job already submitted, to reconfigure a printer remotely, or to learn which settings an administrator is allowed to change.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3380 adds Set-Printer-Attributes, Set-Job-Attributes and Get-Printer-Supported-Values, plus new attributes, three out-of-band values and one new status code. Each set request is all-or-nothing.
tldr.outcome: A user can fix a pending job instead of cancelling and resubmitting it, and an administrator can reconfigure a printer over IPP. Support is optional. The RFC updates RFC 2910 and RFC 2911 and has not been obsoleted.

today: RFC 3380 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 2910 and RFC 2911. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it, and its operations remain OPTIONAL for implementations.

sections.title: What This Extension Adds
sections.content:
The Internet Printing Protocol (IPP) is an application-level protocol for distributed printing. This RFC is an OPTIONAL extension to IPP/1.0 and IPP/1.1. It defines three new operations: Set-Printer-Attributes, Set-Job-Attributes and Get-Printer-Supported-Values.

The two Set operations modify Printer objects and Job objects. They can be used by end users, operators and administrators, subject to access rights. The third operation returns the values a printer will accept when its xxx-supported attributes are set. It MUST be supported if the implementation lets any xxx-supported Printer attribute be set.

The RFC also defines nine new Printer Description attributes, two new operation attributes, three out-of-band values and one new status code. They are covered in the sections below.
sections.eli5: Printers already knew how to take a job and print it. This note adds three new buttons: change a job, change the printer, and ask the printer what choices it has.

sections.title: Requirements and Use Cases
sections.content:
The RFC states two needs. First, an end user or operator needs to modify a job that is in the pending or pending-held state. The example given is a user who forgets to ask for finishings of staple and would otherwise have to cancel and resubmit. An operator might also change a job because the requested media has run out and policy is to print on a comparable medium.

Second, a system administrator needs to re-configure or change the policy of a printer remotely. Examples in the text include adding named media to the supported media list, removing Cancel-Job from the supported operations, replacing no-value placeholders after installing a printer, and updating the media-ready attribute when the media in a tray changes.
sections.eli5: Sometimes you forget to ask for staples, or the paper you picked ran out. It is much easier to fix the job than to throw it away and start over.

sections.title: Set-Printer-Attributes
sections.content:
This operation (operation-id 0x0013) replaces attribute values on a Printer object. The client must supply the printer-uri target and a group of Printer attributes. For multi-valued (1setOf) attributes, the supplied values replace all existing values.

The Printer validates the request before changing anything. The attribute must be supported, must not be READ-ONLY, must be settable in this implementation, must carry values the printer supports, and must not conflict with other Printer attributes, including ones set in the same request. If any attribute fails, the Printer MUST reject the whole operation. The operation is atomic: all supplied attributes are set or none are.

The optional document-format operation attribute selects which document format a change applies to. Attributes listed in document-format-varying-attributes change only for that format, and other attributes change for all formats. The Printer MUST accept the operation when printer-state is idle or stopped, and SHOULD accept it while processing. The user must be an operator or administrator.

If a request changes an xxx-default attribute, the new value MUST be among the xxx-supported values, or the same request must also supply a new xxx-supported that includes it. Otherwise the Printer rejects the request.
sections.eli5: The printer checks your whole list of changes first. If even one change is not allowed, it does none of them, so it never ends up half changed.

sections.title: Set-Job-Attributes
sections.content:
This operation (operation-id 0x0014) is almost identical to Set-Printer-Attributes but is aimed at a Job object. The job is identified either by a job URI or by a printer URI plus a job-id. The caller must be the job owner or an operator or administrator.

Validation works as if the job had been submitted again with the new values, the deleted attributes removed and ipp-attribute-fidelity set to true. If that submission would be accepted, the Set is accepted. Otherwise it is rejected and the job is unchanged. If the job was submitted without a supported attribute, the Set adds it.

A client can remove a job attribute by supplying the delete-attribute out-of-band value. The effect is the same as if the attribute had never been supplied, so the printer's defaults apply again. Deleting an attribute that is not present is ignored.

The job state controls the result. A pending or pending-held job accepts the change and may move between those two states depending on whether needed resources are ready. A processing or processing-stopped job returns successful-ok or client-error-not-possible depending on the implementation. A completed, canceled or aborted job always returns client-error-not-possible.
sections.eli5: You can change your job while it is still waiting in line. Once it is being printed it depends, and once it is finished you are too late.

sections.title: Get-Printer-Supported-Values and admin-define
sections.content:
Get-Printer-Supported-Values (operation-id 0x0015) takes the same request attributes as Get-Printer-Attributes but returns only xxx-supported attributes, and only those the printer allows to be set. It returns the values the implementation inherently supports, not the extra values an administrator added. It requires administrator access rights, while Get-Printer-Attributes needs only end-user rights.

The admin-define out-of-band value appears in this response as one value of an xxx-supported attribute. It tells the client that an administrator may add arbitrary values of the name syntax to that attribute. The RFC lists media-supported, job-hold-until-supported and job-sheets-supported as IPP/1.1 attributes where this applies. A Printer MUST NOT return admin-define in a Get-Printer-Attributes response, because that response shows what an end user can ask for in a job.

If admin-define is absent, the Printer MUST NOT accept a Set value that is not one of the explicit keyword or name values returned.
sections.eli5: Before you rearrange the menu, you ask the kitchen what dishes it can really cook. A special note on the list can say that you may also invent new named dishes.

sections.title: New Attributes, Values and Status Code
sections.content:
Two operation attributes, printer-message-from-operator and job-message-from-operator, let an operator attach a message when pausing, resuming, purging, cancelling, holding, releasing or restarting. They are not supported on the Set operations themselves. In those, the client sets the matching Printer or Job Description attribute directly. Setting the printer message also updates printer-message-time and printer-message-date-time.

The new Printer Description attributes include printer-settable-attributes-supported and job-settable-attributes-supported, which list what is settable (or none), and document-format-varying-attributes. A group of printer-xri-supported and three xri- attributes lets a client set a printer's URIs, authentication and security values together. Each member of printer-xri-supported has xri-uri, xri-authentication and xri-security. The Printer MUST then also set the three READ-ONLY IPP/1.1 attributes printer-uri-supported, uri-authentication-supported and uri-security-supported, so they never end up inconsistent.

The new status code is client-error-attributes-not-settable (0x0413). It is returned with the not-settable out-of-band value for attributes that are READ-ONLY or not settable here, and nothing is changed.
sections.eli5: It adds sticky notes the operator can leave on a printer or job, a way to change the printer's web addresses and security settings together, and a new error that says that setting cannot be changed.

sections.title: Conformance and Registrations
sections.content:
Both Set operations are OPTIONAL, and either can be supported without the other. A Printer that supports Set-Printer-Attributes MUST also support printer-settable-attributes-supported, the not-settable value in responses and the new status code, and MUST support Get-Printer-Supported-Values if any xxx-supported attribute is settable. A Printer that supports Set-Job-Attributes MUST support job-settable-attributes-supported, not-settable, delete-attribute and the new status code.

The IANA section registers the three operations, their operations-supported enum values, the new attributes and keywords, the status code and the three out-of-band values. Appendices A and B are normative tables of which attribute values may be set and which are returned by Get-Printer-Supported-Values.
sections.eli5: Printers do not have to offer these features. But if a printer offers one, it also has to offer the pieces that make it safe and understandable.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
RFC 3380 points to the security discussion in RFC 2911 (client authentication, server authentication and operation privacy) and adds a new threat: letting clients modify Printer and Job attributes could lead to denial of service.

A malicious user could alter the policy stored in the Printer attributes. The RFC's example is removing all values from document-format-supported, so the printer refuses every job. A malicious user could also change another user's job, for example by setting copies to a large number. The remedy is strong client authentication with printer access control, limiting who has administrator or operator privileges, and storing the authentication with each job so that only its owner can modify it.
sections.eli5: If anyone could change the rules, a prankster could make the printer refuse everything or print a thousand copies of your page. So the printer should check who you are first.
